name: Zim Laboratories Ltd
title: Zim Laboratories Ltd - 541400 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Zim Labs Q4 FY26 revenue INR 1,053 mn with EBITDA margin 12.7%; FY26 revenue flat at INR 3,744 mn as EU GMP and MENA disruptions weighed.
summary.overview: Management said CAPA is substantially complete and a German/Portuguese EU GMP re-inspection ran 4–7 May 2026, with a positive wrap-up but no written report yet. Q4 operating income was about INR 1,053 mn, EBITDA about INR 134 mn (12.7%) and PAT INR 37 mn, with exports about 82% of income. FY26 EBITDA was about INR 414 mn and PAT INR 58 mn, with INR 311 mn spent on BE studies and registrations for the NIP and OTF pipeline. Guidance is limited: FY27 base business guided only as roughly flat-to-slightly-up in H1, with a stronger outlook contingent on EU GMP reinstatement.

segments.name: Exports / core pharma (generic)
segments.commentary: Exports ~82% of Q4 operating income and described as the dominant driver; management cited sequential growth each quarter. Regulated-market sales constrained by EU GMP non-compliance.

segments.name: NIP + OTF (innovative platforms)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 254 mn (22% of income), sequentially improved; YoY softer as approvals are linked to EU GMP reinstatement. Licensing-fee milestones (dossier submission, MA receipt) stalled and expected to resume after EU GMP.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals (legacy, Middle East)
segments.commentary: Declined YoY (analyst cited INR 95 cr to INR 75 cr, not confirmed) due to Middle East disruption; management guides 10-15% annual growth over the next 24 months.

segments.name: Domestic institutional
segments.commentary: Declined YoY due to missed institutional tenders; company now marketing NIP and OTF products in India privately. No figure given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 base business: H1 guided at roughly the same level as current, with a modest increase; fuller guidance only after EU GMP reinstatement.
Post EU GMP, management expects regulated-market revenue from Q4 FY27; no quantified revenue guidance given.
EBITDA margin: management projects mid-to-upper teens once regulated markets scale (analyst cited ~20% target in 24-36 months; management called upper teens a fair assumption).
No further capex expected for the 17 NIP+OTF products; heavy capex cycle near completion, with preferential issue proceeds going to capacity and CAPA infrastructure.
Borrowings to stay flat and finance cost to remain similar in FY27 per finance director.
Management declined to give NIP+OTF peak revenue or FY27/FY28 percentage guidance.
capex_capacity: EU GMP re-inspection (German and Portuguese authorities) held 4–7 May 2026; draft report expected in days, though a later Q&A answer said about a month; CAPA process expected to complete within about two months.
Alternate CMO/toll partner selected for Star Product 1 and urology product; variation filings to add the site to be applied soon, with revenue allocation not finalised.
Enzyme (gastrointestinal) product: new dedicated block built; can also be made in existing plant once EU GMP is restored. Sildenafil OTF supplies to Europe stopped pending reinstatement.
Preferential issue of INR 35 cr to Florintree Trinix LLP at INR 73.46/share, for an enzyme NIP suite, nutraceutical plant expansion and CAPA; company pointed to exchange filing for deployment detail.
Australia TGA inspection held in the period; TGA accreditation expected, enabling supply from own site and the alternate site.
demand_pricing: Dabigatran capsules received EU marketing authorisation in May 2026; management cited a ~USD 400 mn EU market and Italy at ~USD 60 mn; commercialisation tied to EU GMP reinstatement; no partner named.
Anticoagulant product approved in Italy via DCP procedure; partners being finalised for Europe.
Pancreatin (enzyme) shortage in Europe expected to continue; commercialisation targeted for Q4 FY27 subject to EU GMP.
Five NIP/OTF products approved but not yet commercially supplied; shipments targeted from around January after EU GMP restoration.
Management expects the 17-product NIP+OTF basket commercialised in about 24 months; regulated vs ROW split guided at roughly 30:20 of the 50% innovative share.
Management expects ROW and pharmerging to set a minimum run rate of about INR 16-18 cr per quarter for NIP (analyst's read of eight-quarter history; management said this is the floor).
Domestic decline attributed to missed institutional tenders; no quantified share given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIP+OTF revenue fall and what products are most affected; what happens after EU GMP is restored?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIP products for the regulated market are awaiting EU GMP certification, expected around Q2, with revenue from Q4. No addressable revenue guidance was given because timing depends on MA receipt and customer relaunch.

qa_highlights.question: Market size and timing for dabigatran capsules, and who is the partner?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a ~USD 400 mn European market, Italy ~USD 60 mn, with commercialisation planned once EU GMP is back on track; some contracts signed and interested partners, no partner named.

qa_highlights.question: Root cause of the July 2025 EU GMP failure and reinspection scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to data-integrity observations on EudraGMDP, over-reliance on manual documentation, and said CAPA added digitalisation, e-logbooks and tightened QA; the process was overseen by consultants over six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Margin differential and revenue on the alternate CMO for Star Product 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin impact would be marginal, with toll manufacturing charges slightly above in-house cost; revenue allocation not yet finalised pending site approval.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% EBITDA margin achievable in 24-36 months, and is 17-product scale-up feasible without more capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projects upper-teens EBITDA margins once regulated markets scale and said no further capex is needed for the 17 products, as heavy capex is near completion.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q4 licensing fee income absent and when does it resume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said licensing milestones tied to EU GMP (dossier submission and MA) stopped; they should resume once EU GMP is restored.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 'draft report' and disclosure of inspection observations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to classify observations, saying the closing meeting was informal and the written report is awaited; said it expects no critical observations, though this is an assumption.

risks_watch: EU GMP reinstatement timing: management guided to a 2-3 month window, and the formal inspection report and any CAPA requirements are still pending; regulated revenue, Australia supply and licensing milestones all depend on it.
Inspection classification (major/critical) not disclosed; a delayed or adverse report would push out NIP/OTF launches and the dabigatran and pancreatin plans.
Middle East (MENA) disruption since ~Feb 2026 hurting nutraceuticals and export revenue; recovery timing uncertain.
Dependence on alternate CMO/toll site for Star Product 1 pending variation approval; revenue allocation not yet disclosed.
Domestic institutional tender losses; management says revenue should stabilise.
Margin expansion depends on regulated-market ramp; Q4 EBITDA margin of 12.7% and FY26 PAT of INR 58 mn remain thin.
Debt and finance cost held flat in FY27; deleveraging path not defined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the EU GMP re-inspection outcome and timelines, but evasive on quantitative guidance (NIP+OTF share, peak revenue, inspection observation classification), citing the informal closing meeting and awaited written report.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we have substantially completed our CAPA implementation.
We estimate a revenue impact of approximately INR 20 crore that we could have otherwise achieved from this region.
We are assuming, and we are projecting upper teens as our EBITDA margins once everything kind of starts going on in the regulated markets.
We are not in any plans to increase borrowings any further.

adds.what: Enzyme (gastrointestinal) dedicated block built; can also be made in existing plant once EU GMP restored
Nutraceutical plant expansion and CAPA funded by INR 35 cr preferential issue

growth.why: FY27 H1 base business guided only at roughly current levels with a modest increase, no numeric FY27 guidance; regulated-market growth from Q4 FY27 depends on EU GMP reinstatement (re-inspection outcome pending), and the only firm numbers are a 10-15% nutraceutical growth target over 24 months and an EBITDA margin aspiration of upper teens, backed by vague or unquantified capacity and orders.
